title: Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" in the weeks before Star Wars Zero Company's launch
text:
Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" prior to the game's release.
A representative for Bit Reactor told Game File it was a "difficult decision" made "before it was clear how the launch would go." They also clarified that it was not influenced by publisher Electronic Arts or Star Wars license holder Disney.
Zero Company has been positively received by players and critics , and is currently ranked second on Steam's top sellers list .
Sources told Game File that 80% of Bit Reactor's staff were furloughed, leaving a skeleton crew to address any post-launch bugs for Zero Company.
The decision was reportedly due to Bit Reactor having "run out of most of its money just ahead of the launch of its first game."
Former senior technical artist Zachariah Scott claimed on LinkedIn that the studio was "concealing the fact that the team was furloughed weeks ago."
Scott also told Game File that budgets were "tight" during his tenure and that studio founder Greg Foertsch "often mentioned hoping to secure a new game deal to keep things going."
Scott recalled that developers wanted more lightsaber animations but were told there was not enough budget. He described the project as developed with "shocking austerity."
Bit Reactor's representative said the studio "hoped to bring furloughed workers back, suggesting that a successful launch of the game could be impactful."
However, Scott noted that staff he spoke with "were less confident that even if there were returns, that all who were furloughed would get their old jobs again."
The furloughs were also referenced in a 2024 lawsuit filed by former chief operating officer Alison Kelly, which noted the studio also "terminated contractors."
The filing centres on whether Kelly is a co-owner of Bit Reactor or if Foertsch is the sole owner, with Kelly alleging that Foertsch pushed her out of the company.
Kelly referenced a draft operating agreement from April 2021 that proposed splitting the company's shares among Foertsch, Kelly, and early co-founder Tom Whittaker. Whittaker and another co-founder, Steve Meyer, have since left the studio.
Foertsch's legal representatives argued the draft agreement was never signed, indicating Kelly was not an owner, and claimed she was terminated for poor job performance. Kelly denied these claims and is seeking over $20 million in damages.

title: Rovio closes Copenhagen studio following shut down of Sonic Blitz
text:
Rovio has closed its Copenhagen studio after cancelling its mobile title Sonic Blitz.
A spokesperson told Mobilegamer.biz that, as the redundancy process is ongoing, they cannot confirm the exact number of staff affected. However, approximately 20 employees were working on Sonic Blitz.
"The decision to discontinue our operations in Copenhagen has been extremely difficult," the spokesperson said. "We fully recognise the impact this has on our team, especially given the ongoing challenges within the broader games industry."
"For team members who we cannot allocate to a new project within Rovio, we will provide a comprehensive transition package, including dedicated outplacement services and wellbeing support to assist them in securing their next career opportunities."
Rovio CEO and Sega West COO Alexandre Pelletier-Normand said that it "need[ed] to concentrate our bets both in terms of the games that we're making and where we're making them."
"When [Sonic Blitz] was introduced into the brand, we felt that this was a great addition and one that could please the Sonic fandom," he said.
"That was the hypothesis. And in mobile, it looks great on paper, and then you just need to validate it, and it seems that retention hasn't been really good for us, which is one of the first steps. We need to see people engage with the game for a long period of time."
Pelletier-Normand continued: "I still am convinced that there is a way to reach more players on mobile with Sonic, it turns out that it's much more complicated than I think both Sega and Rovio thought. We're still very proud of the game, very proud of what the team achieved, but it didn’t work."
Sonic Blitz soft launched in 2025 in the Philippines and Brazil , but was shut down last month . Rovio stated that this decision was part of a "broader change" at the studio.
"We want to be clear that this decision is not a reflection of the passion, creativity or effort that went into making Sonic Blitz, nor the amazing support we received from our community throughout the development of the game," the developer said.
Sega acquired Rovio for $776 million in 2023. Earlier this year, Sega reported a $200 million impairment on the acquisition cost after profitability "fell below the initial forecast."
Sega reported challenges integrating Rovio's Beacon technology with its own mobile titles.
"We found that the operational and marketing methods and approaches significantly differ from Rovio titles and new mobile games are yet to fully exploit Beacon," said Sega CEO Haruki Satomi.
"Consequently, we have unfortunately not achieved the level of results that had been expected prior to the acquisition."

title: Gamescom 2026 attendance rose 6% to 368,000 visitors
text:
Gamescom 2026 attracted 368,000 visitors from 131 countries, a 6% increase over the previous year.
A total of 1,743 companies from 66 countries exhibited, up 11% from 2025. International exhibitors accounted for 72% of participants, with 48 country pavilions representing 41 countries.
Brazil, Canada, and the US saw the strongest growth. Over 36,000 trade visitors attended, with about half coming from outside Germany.
Gamescom Dev attendance rose 15% to 6,200 visitors. The conference, which took place prior to Gamescom, featured 397 speakers, 238 sessions, and 18 stages.
More than 2,500 companies from 95 countries participated, along with 57 partners and exhibitors across Gamescom Dev and its indie expo.
GamesIndustry.biz spoke with Gamescom Dev managing director Frederik Hammes about the results of this year's Gamescom Dev survey , which identified smaller studios as the largest growth opportunity in the games market.
Gamescom's digital content reached over 624 million global views by Saturday evening, including 78 million for Opening Night Live . The Gamescom Awesome Indies Show attracted more than 302,000 viewers, a growth of over 670%.
Digital community adventure Gamescom Epix generated 6.2 million page views, up approximately 9% from the previous year.
"In 2026, Gamescom has delivered an impressive statement about its role as the central platform for the international games industry," said German Games Industry Association managing director Felix Falk.
"Many of last year's record figures were surpassed, especially in terms of international participation and the number of exhibitors. The drive for the future can be felt here – it's what again propels the industry forward this year despite the challenges – and what makes the gamescom atmosphere so unique."
President and chief executive officer of Koelnmesse Gerald Böse added: "Gamescom brings people from all over the world together, combining the economic and social significance of games on a scale like no other. This was an extremely successful Gamescom, and we are delighted by the event's strong international character. It shows gamescom's ever-growing importance as the leading platform for everyone who plays, develops and creates games."
Gamescom 2027 will take place from August 25 to 29, with Gamescom Dev running from August 23 to 24.

title: UKIE launches Discord-backed Go To Market Academy, a business program to support early-stage indie devs
text:
UKIE has partnered with Discord and GameFlex to launch the Go To Market Academy , a business program to support UK-based indie studios.
The Academy aims to provide early-stage developers with the tools to build go-to-market strategies and sustainable communities.
The program consists of six online modules covering diagnostics and insights, marketing strategy and campaign execution, using Discord for community engagement, and studio branding. Industry guest speakers will also participate.
Open to 10 to 12 studios, the program begins with an in-person session at EGX at MCM Comic Con in London next month. Online sessions will follow throughout November and early December.
Sessions will conclude with another in-person event, where participating studios will present their go-to-market plans developed through "a shared case study over the course of the programme."
Interested studios can apply here , with applications closing on September 30, 2026.
"Go-to-market planning is where a lot of promising games fall down, not because studios lack good ideas, but because they haven't had the time or support to build the audience and community that gives those ideas a chance to flourish," said UKIE CEO Nick Poole.
"The Go To Market Academy gives indie studios the space to work through that properly, with direct input from Discord on a platform that’s become central to how games communities actually form and grow."
Discord director of public policy EMEA Mauro Sanna added: "The UK's indie games scene is full of talent and opportunity, and we're delighted to partner with UKIE to help it thrive. We're excited to help this group of UK developers learn how to make the most of Discord to connect with our highly engaged gaming audience, build communities and grow their games."

title: Jobs roundup: September 2026 | Amir Satvat joins 1Up Ventures as a general partner
text:
It can be difficult keeping track of the various comings and goings in the games industry, which is why we compile them in semi-regular round-ups.
If you have new appointments or transitions in your company that belong here, please send the names of appointees, new role and company, and prior role and company to newhires@gamesindustry.biz .
Amir Satvat joins 1Up Ventures as a general partner
Amir Satvat has joined 1Up Ventures as general manager. Satvat previously served as business development director at Tencent Games.
He is also the founder and leader of Always Supporting the Games Community (ASGC), a resource of helping people find jobs in the games industry.
"I wanted to feel a more direct connection between the things I could influence and do with a team and putting people back to work," said Satvat. "I wanted to see more people's dreams of making games come true because of something I did. I also hoped I could work in a setting focused on smaller studios, because I love games of that size so much, and in a setting built around community first.
"My final wish was to work with colleagues who share the same values and integrity I try to hold myself to. In accepting the team’s invitation to join 1Up, I am seeing all of these wishes realised."
He added: "1Up is a very important player in the games ecosystem, and I want to see its unique approach to games investing survive for as long as possible."
Housemarque co-founder and managing director Ilari Kuittinen steps down
Housemarque co-founder and managing director Ilari Kuittinen has stepped down after 31 years at the studio. Kuittinen co-founded Housemarque with Harri Tikkanen in 1995 after merging their companies Bloodhouse and Terramarque.
"Looking back, I feel immensely fortunate," said Kuittinen. "We had the luck of being in the right place at the right time during three decades of incredible industry growth, allowing us to stay fiercely independent for 26 years before finding a home within the PlayStation Studios family."
"We have been planning this leadership transition carefully behind the scenes. On July 1, Sami 'Haxu' Hakala officially stepped into the managing director role, and I have continued supporting him and the leadership team until today to ensure complete operational continuity and stability. Housemarque’s strategy and creative vision are in exceptional hands."
Tamara Feiman appointed CEO of Lion Studios
Tamara Feiman has been appointed CEO at Tripledot Studios' Lion Studios. Feiman previously served as publishing general manager, having started her career at Lion Studios in 2020 as EMEA business development lead.
"I joined Lion six years ago," said Feiman. "Since then, I've had the privilege of growing alongside the company through its biggest successes, challenges and transformations. But what has always made Lion special is how we work with our partner studios. Together, we've taken risks, learned quickly and turned great ideas into games played by millions.
"And Lion has never been about one person. I'm fortunate to work alongside an incredible team across publishing, growth, product, engineering and market intelligence, as well as our talented studio partners around the world."
Heather Sangria | Community manager, Sega of America
Heather Sangria has joined Sega of America as appointed community manager. Sangria previously served as contract social strategist and community lead at One More Game. She also worked at Undead Labs as digital strategy and community manager.
Emily Rose Chen | Senior product manager, Call of Duty, Activision Blizzard
Emily Rose Chen has been promoted to senior product manager for Call of Duty at Activision Blizzard. Chen previously served as product manager, having joined as a financial analyst in 2020.
Scot McCarron | Senior director, product management, Call of Duty
Scot McCarron has been promoted to senior director of product management for Call of Duty at Activision Blizzard. McCarron previously served as director of product management on Call of Duty, having joined Activision in 2018 as product marketing manager for emerging franchises.

title: Brian Ward steps down as Savvy Games Group CEO
text:
Brian Ward is stepping down as CEO of Savvy Games Group, according to a staff note obtained by Bloomberg .
"As Savvy embarks on its next period of transformational growth, this is the right time for new leadership for that evolution," Ward wrote.
Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and head of its International Investments Division, will serve as interim acting CEO.
Ward has served as CEO since Savvy Games Group was established in 2021, overseeing a $37.8 billion investment to expand Saudi Arabia's presence in the global games industry.
Savvy Games Group was set up and is wholly owned by the PIF, which Ward previously described as being part of Saudi Arabia's "economic diversification and social transformation."
During Ward's tenure, Savvy acquired several studios, including Moonton from Bytedance for $6 million earlier this year and Scopely for $4.9 billion in 2023 .
Before joining Savvy, Ward held leadership roles at Electronic Arts, Xbox, and Activision.
Ward's decision to leave Savvy came just a month after EA was acquired for $55 billion by a consortium led by the PIF.

title: Housemarque co-founder Ilari Kuittinen exits from studio
text:
'Strive to be a better professional, and a better human being.'
Ilari Kuittinen, co-founder and CEO of PlayStation-owned game studio Housemarque , has announced his exit from the company after 31 years of game development.
Kuittinen announced the move in a post on LinkedIn , where explained the company has been preparing for this transition for several months. One major stabilizing move was the appointment of Sami "Haxu" Hakala as Housemarque managing director. Kuittinen said he has spent the time since then supporting "him and the leadership team" to ensure "complete operational continuinity and stability."
"Housemarque's strategy and creative vision are in exceptional hands," he said.
His departure comes after a very long run with the studio—a rarity in the video game industry. Kuittinen co-founded the company with Harri Tikkanen in 1995 after the two merged their existing companies: Bloodhouse and Terramarque. Today, the company is the oldest active game studio in Finland.
Related: Report: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward departs company
Under his leadership, Housemarque built publishing relationships with companies like Take-Two Interactive, Ubisoft, and most consequentially, Sony Computer Entertainment (today known as Sony Interactive Entertainment). Sony first published Super Stardust HD in 2007 on the PlayStation 3, and the two companies' working relationship would see them partnering on exclusives like Resogun and Matterfall . Then in 2021, Sony purchased Housemarque, bringing it into the fold of PlayStation Studios. It's since released Returnal and Saros under that banner.
This is one of several leadership changes that have taken place at PlayStation Studios over the last few years, with studio heads and co-founders like Ted Price , Brian Fleming , and Evan Wells retiring after similar decades-long runs at the helm of their companies. Now Kuittinen joins their ranks with the promise that he is taking "a rare and well-deserved breather."
"Remember our guiding light: strive to be a better professional, and a better human being," he said in a closing bit of advice. "Take care of each other, speak with courage, and keep pushing the boundaries of what games can be."

One source claimed that around 80 percent of the Bit Reactor team has been furloughed. Another said that only a "skeleton crew" remains on active payroll at the U.S. studio.
On LinkedIn , a former Bit Reactor employee who claims to have been fired "after being involuntarily put on medical leave" and then prevented from sharing those facts with friends and colleagues, suggested the studio has been "trying to keep the team in a holding pattern with good vibes and more empty promises."
Notably, they alleged that furloughed staff members have been "cut off from any possible profit sharing."
Related: Report: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward departs company
A Bit Reactor spokesperson told Game File the company hopes to reinstate furloughed employees and restore their pay if Star Wars Zero Company proves successful.
It's unclear how well the EA-published video game has performed across all platforms, although it remains one of the top-selling titles on Steam (in terms of revenue) at the time of writing.

title: Paradox Interactive's Afterworld wants to entice new players to grand strategy with tasty RPG hooks
text:
Game director Dan Lind explains the appeal of strategy in grand strategy games, and how to invite new players into a sprawling game.
One of the appeals of the grand strategy genre is the awesome sense of scale: you're building a sprawling civilization from the ground up, making key decisions on allocating resources and making plays to expand your influence. For those who can immerse themselves in games such as Sid Meier's Civilization, Hearts of Iron, and Crusader Kings, it can offer unparalleled moments of storytelling and agency—but for less experienced players, just getting started can be daunting.
That's where the upcoming grand strategy game Afterworld from Paradox Interactive is looking to shake things up. While still very much about the experience of cultivating a civilization in the making, Afterworld brings sprawling 4x4 and grand strategy gameplay to a post-apocalyptic setting, where all factions—known as tribes—will have to learn how to survive and thrive within a world slowly rebuilding itself. It's a game that puts discovery and cultural development front and center, alongside mutants, cyborg billionaires, and rival tribes with a taste for human flesh.
Related: Warlock's magic system was built on game-bending player choices
After getting a first look at Afterworld , game director Dan Lind of Paradox Development Studio explained that this post-apocalyptic sandbox is the team’s effort to open up the grand strategy genre to new players. One secret to Afterworld ’s recipe: a keen focus on role-playing elements is key to pushing the genre even further.
"We have always been very focused on the audience that we have with our games, and I hope all of them will like this too, but since we've grown as a company, we want to broaden the audience more as well," said game director Dan Lind. "When it comes to games like this, it's always about that 4X experience of starting small and expanding as a necessity, but making that easy for all players to get into can be a challenge. I'm not sure how I would do this with Hearts of Iron, honestly, because it's like you're starting in the middle of history. But that's why I like this version of a post-apocalyptic setting [with Afterworld ], it's like we're restarting history and putting all players in that space forging that path into the unknown."
The game's setting is North America, centuries after total ruin. The remaining clusters of survivors are isolated from one another, with some cultures living in secluded bunkers, surviving on the surface in makeshift towns, or living in protected cities in service to former rich men (turned cyborg deities), the player's chosen tribe will steadily branch out into the larger world. On this new path of rediscovery, players will establish and expand territory, interact with other surviving groups, and build up a new civilization of their own making—all while trying to co-exist or face off against others who may have conflicting interests.
Related: How you (yes, you) can benefit from 1-on-1 synchronous playtesting
Paradox Development Studio has been at the forefront of the grand strategy genre for a long time, with recent hits like Stellaris , Hearts of Iron IV , and Crusader Kings III . With Crusader Kings III in particular, the team not only innovated on the complex diplomacy and kingdom-building gameplay for a Middle Ages setting, but it also further emphasized that one of the great strengths of the genre is storytelling. Players weave fascinating yearns as they shape their own nations and characters, and deal with the causality of their choices.
For Afterworld , the developers were keen to focus on player choice within a post-apocalyptic setting. It certainly taps into the complex expansion systems and branching threads of choices found in other games in the genre. Afterworld puts more of a focus on getting your tribe to a place where they'll be able not just to survive and build a network of communities, but also evolve as a culture. Of course, what that looks like in-game is entirely up to the player.
Related: How Forbidden Solitaire brought solitaire games to the forefront
"That's something I'm betting on a lot, it's why I decided to make the tribe origins in Afterworld a bit like building your backstory of sorts," said the game director. "Instead of going the Stellaris route where it's a lot of settings to tune, we're gonna try to ease you into playing a role-playing game with your tribe, essentially. I think for people who are not used to how a grand strategy game works, it can be quite hard to understand that you can do anything and to find out what your own goal is. With Afterworld , it's gonna make you adapt and stay in the moment. I think at some point you'll realize you've actually set goals for yourself and you're able to do stuff. So I'm hoping we'll be able to attract people who are invested in [the] story and won't have to think too much about number crunching."
Playing the early stages of Afterworld as the Shelterborn tribe felt akin to a strategic roadtrip. One tribe we got to see in action was the Shelterborn, a community of survivors who lived in vaults and were isolated from the changed surface world. By stepping out of their decaying shelter—which explodes after a few phases pass—this particular faction has to figure out how to navigate an unfamiliar world. This starts with building safe havens and securing resources, but eventually expands to communicating with other roaming tribes, and even the nearby warlords who may demand your loyalty.
One aspect that jumped out was the worldbuilding and the sense of discovery as you slowly chart the world. This leads into one of Afterworld 's most intriguing concepts: the tribe's core ideas. Presented in an expansive menu that draws on similar abstract character-growth paths from Disco Elysium , the player tribe will expand its knowledge and skills based on which survivors and events it comes into contact with. A new idea introduced at the right time can change the makeup of an entire tribe. Based on which ideas you want to pursue and develop: such as foraging, old-world technology, or even cannibalism if you so inclined—you'll build your tribe's core ethos, which the player's chosen council will pass on to others.
In keeping with Lind's view that Afterworld is a role-playing game, the core tribes serve as jumping-off points for players to evolve, changing based on the discoveries they make while playing. It's not just about the experience of building an empire and seizing territory through battles or wits, but it's also about how your tribune is building its future and way of life. Whether that's about a sheltered community building a communist civilization that dismantles slavery and injustice, or a community that values old-world technology (and perhaps slowly developing a taste for human flesh), there are many different directions a player's journey can go.
For Lind, Afterworld is a concept that's been in the making for a long time, and he feels he's in a position to make it now thanks to the success of his previous game-director work on Hearts of Iron IV and Crusader Kings III .
"I've had this concept for Afterworld in the backlog for some time, even before I started work on Hearts of Iron IV, " said Lind. "I had sketches of this game, but it felt too experimental for us to dare gamble on. I had to deliver on some games before someone lets me do a totally different grand strategy game like this, right? I do think it has massive potential, in that people who might not be into the other games can find this one. Stellaris was a big step for us when we did that, because that was a game where people who saw us produce it had never played our games, so it's also a way into the other games for them, right? I'm hoping this is similar, but tapping into a different audience as well. You don't work on something like this without being passionate about it for a long time. It's a huge commitment and a big responsibility to take on, right?"

title: Sega-owned Rovio is shutting down its Copenhagen studio
text:
The closure follows the cancellation of Sonic Blitz and the exact number of redundancies are yet to be confirmed.
Sega-owned Rovio, best known for the Angry Birds franchise, is shutting down its Copenhagen studio following the cancellation of Sonic Blitz .
A Rovio spokesperson confirmed the news to Mobilegamer.biz last week. In a statement, the company said that "following a redundancy process, Rovio will discontinue all its operations in Denmark."
According to the statement, the process is still ongoing, so Rovio hasn't confirmed an exact number of redundancies. That being said, "around 20 employees" worked on the now canceled Sonic Blitz project, the spokesperson added.
"For team members who we cannot allocate to a new project within Rovio, we will provide a comprehensive transition package, including dedicated outplacement services and wellbeing support to assist them in securing their next career opportunities," the company told Mobilegamer.
The statement goes on to say that the decision has been "extremely difficult," and that Rovio fully recognizes the impact this has on the team, especially "given the ongoing challenges" within the broader game industry .
Related: Report: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward departs company
For context, Sonic Blitz was a hybrid runner and card collection game for mobile devices. In an interview, Sega West COO and Rovio CEO Alex Pelletier-Normand told Mobilegamer that retention didn't meet expectations, saying that the studio needs to "see people engage with the game for a long period of time."
Sega completed its acquisition of Rovio back in mid August of 2023 . The company closed down subsidiary Studio Lumi four months later, and it shut down its Moomin mobile game in April of 2024. Then, in October of last year, the company laid off 36 employees , saying it was reorganizing internally and "tightening relations" with Sega. Earlier this year, Sega lamented its failure to make more from its collaboration with Rovio.
"I still am convinced that there is a way to reach more players on mobile with Sonic, it turns out that it's much more complicated than I think both Sega and Rovio thought," Pelletier-Normand told Mobilegamer. "We're still very proud of the game, very proud of what the team achieved, but it didn't work."

title: Supercell’s acquisition of Merge Mansion maker Metacore to be finalised this month
text:
Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year , revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.
“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”
Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.
Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates , the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.
Supercell is a long-term investor and partner to fellow Finnish firm Metacore. In January 2023, Metacore acquired failed Supercell soft launch game Everdale  and attempted to rework and relaunch the game under its ownership, but killed the game in September 2024 .

title: Eddy Cue to take over the App Store as Phil Schiller steps down
text:
Longtime Apple exec Phil Schiller has stepped down from running Apple’s App Store and its product events.
Bloomberg reports that oversight of the App Store moves to the services division led by Eddy Cue, who ran the store himself before Schiller took it over in 2015.
Carson Oliver stays on to run the App Store day-to-day, but now reports to Cue rather than Schiller. Ann Thai’s team, which was set up to work with developers, payments companies and alternative distributors amid Apple’s many court battles, will now report into Oliver.
Apple Arcade is also moving into the same reporting line, meaning Arcade lead Alex Rofman moves under Oliver. It brings the subscription service under the same umbrella as the wider App Store.
Oliver and Thai took on their current roles as part of the reorg that saw App Store head Matt Fischer leave in 2024 . The exec changes land just as John Ternus takes over as CEO, with Tim Cook moving to executive chairman after 15 years running the company .
Bloomberg reports that Schiller, 66, is staying on with his Apple Fellow title but has no fixed new remit. The report suggests that Apple sees the move as a likely step toward retirement. It’s one of several veteran departures Ternus will have to manage as he succeeds Cook, including operations chief Jeff Williams and finance chief Luca Maestri.
Schiller helped build the App Store alongside Steve Jobs and, in recent years, led the executive team handling developer disputes and regulatory pressure over the store’s commission structure, including Apple’s court fight with Epic Games . The App Store is now estimated to generate more than $30bn a year.
Phillip Shoemaker, who built and ran Apple’s app review division from 2009 to 2016, told us in 2023 that Schiller was blocking automation of app review and said bluntly that he “needs to get his meaty paws off the App Store.”
Last week, Apple’s own App Store team shared advice for developers on getting featured at Gamescom, and in particular pushed the ‘try before you buy’ business model as the best option for premium game makers.

title: Korean giant NC has spent $300m on four studios and isn’t stopping there
text:
NC’s Anel Ceman says the Korean giant is looking to buy established mobile studios making $50-100m per year across all genres and business models.
Ceman is the firm’s head of social mobile and had worked in senior roles at Outfit7, Wildlife and Tripledot before taking up a leadership role at the Korean giant.
He’s been busy. In the last year the MMO specialist formerly known as NCsoft has spent over $300m acquiring four mobile game companies – Vietnam’s Lihuhu, Korea-based Springcomes, Moving Eye in Slovenia and Germany’s JustPlay, a rewarded gaming platform founded by several former AppLovin execs.
Across those four studios, NC now runs around 200 live mobile games in total, and it is pulling in all the data from those titles to build a central internal toolset that can manage creative production, live ops, A/B testing, prediction models and more across its portfolio.
“We will keep buying actively,” says Ceman, who notes that the Korean firm is looking to buy up developers working “where the best games are made,” including markets like Japan, China, India and Turkiye.
“We are trying to build or acquire hubs in these strategic regions,” he continues. “We have Europe, Korea and Vietnam already covered.”
Having spent over $200m on JustPlay in March , NC’s next deal may be even bigger, says Ceman. NC is looking for mobile studios with successful live titles pulling in $50-100m a year.
“We look at studios that are profitable, that already have some size, then we can then help them out with scaling,” he says.
“For studios that we acquire, we do not operate them so they are quite independent. Think of it as an operator partner, we provide either financing capital or expertise from me and my team or technology or strategic things that NC built, either AI or live ops or technology infrastructure.”
Ceman is clear that NC is not looking to be an early-stage investor or take punts on new or unproven studios. He is only on the lookout for high potential live games, be they ad-monetised, IAP-based or a mix of both.
“We are building an ecosystem, and to build the whole ecosystem, you need to have the full monetisation spectrum,” he adds.
“That means we have all the data, but then also what works in specific genres or specific categories…so then, if something works for one studio, it can be easily replicated or translated across the whole portfolio. Not everything, but quite a lot of things, can be done in that way.”
NC has said publicly that it intends to build its mobile casual division into a $5bn business by 2030, representing about a third of its total revenue.
“If we look at the last quarter, mobile casual earnings were already 22 percent of total NC revenue,” adds Ceman. “So we are becoming an important pillar in the company.”

title: 17年后，《剑网3》再出发
text:
下午四点，雨后的南沙难得放晴。大湾区文化体育中心的内外已经聚满了从天南海北赶来的人们，五颜六色的门派校服、装满周边的痛包在人群中交错。有人停下来给带来的角色玩偶拍照，有人拉着亲友和Coser合影，也有人在留言板上认真留下自己的游戏ID……相熟的名字在人群中响起，不相识的人们也能因为交换物料迅速聊起来。
距离晚上七点开始的活动还有几个小时，这场属于《剑网3》的庆典，已经提前热闹了起来。
场馆里的留言板上写满了玩家们的祝福
8月28日，《剑网3》十七周年庆典在这里举行，约1.8万名玩家齐聚现场，是《剑网3》历届828周年庆中规模最大的一次。
为什么《剑网3》的周年庆规模会越来越大？
在媒体群访中，《剑网3》系列制作人、玩家们熟悉的“咸鱼”余玉贤被问到了这个问题。他说，理由很简单，“我们每一年都多开一些票，但每一年玩家都喷我们票不够，每一年都是秒空，就得（把场地）再放大点。”
去年，周年庆的现场规模已经到了一个新的节点。“到去年那个规模的时候，我们就发现体育场坐不下了，只开一面台的话。那你必须得开四面台。”于是，今年的828第一次采用了四面舞台，把庆典现场继续放大。
而在此时，《剑网3》也开始谈起下一年，以及更远一些的未来。
■ 十七年后，从50级再出发
发布会是当晚的重头戏，几首歌曲表演结束后，余玉贤在掌声和欢呼声中走上了舞台。没有花太多时间铺垫，他对《剑网3》未来规划给出的第一个答案是：重回五十级。
他宣布，《剑网3》全新50级新世代“苍生铸世”将于10月29日正式公测。届时，角色等级上限将重新回到50级，等级、数值和成长体系也会随之重构。十七年后，“五十级”再次成为这个江湖的新起点。
余玉贤解释，《剑网3》作为一款长线运营的MMO游戏，它的角色等级、装备数值、门派数量和各种系统一路叠加，新玩家想进入这个已经存在多年的江湖，需要面对的门槛也随之增高。他们担心游戏遇到类似的问题，“新玩家永远进不来了。要追老玩家，要么你氪'死'，要么你就肝'死'。”
虽然《剑网3》过去每个赛季都会做一定程度的“洗牌”，缩小新老玩家之间的差距，但这一次的改变显得更为坚决：“我们决定再一次把大家拉进来，（把问题）解决彻底，让我们的这个江湖直接回到当初的时候。”
现场播放的动画短片
今年《剑网3》还提出了“要让老门派重回主角地位”，没有像往年一样宣布上线新门派。
过去，新门派曾经是游戏拉新和回流的重要手段，但随着门派越来越多，职业平衡也变得越来越复杂。余玉贤说，一个新门派上线之后，团队至少要花半年反复调整，“最后还不一定能调平”。而从过去的数据来看，老门派带来的新增和回流已经远大于新门派。于是今年，团队决定先停下来，把已经存在了很多年的门派重新摆回主角的位置。
“‘生态梳理’是好听的说法，其实就是改革。”余玉贤说。
改革的范围也不止门派。PVE、PVP、PVX和社交系统都会一起调整，等级、数值和威名等系统也会被重新梳理。过去那些需要玩家反复投入时间、却不一定真正有趣的部分，会被尽可能压缩，让玩家把时间留给更值得的事情。
当触乐提问，未来的《剑网3》希望探索怎样的MMO发展路径时，余玉贤说了一个有趣的比喻。在他的期望中，未来PVX内容能让《剑网3》这个江湖像一颗“温暖的地球”：玩家可以在这里轻松生活，装扮自己的角色、布置家园、和朋友聊天；而竞技场、攻防战、团本，则像远处的行星，是玩家成长之后可以仰望、也可以选择乘坐飞船前往的地方。
“我在地球成长得差不多时，仰望星空能看到有这么好的追求、（想到）有机会能坐着飞船上去，就可以了。”他强调，目的是建立一套能容纳不同玩家、不同强度追求的分层结构。
这其实也对应着《剑网3》对于玩家在线时间的一种重新理解。过去的MMO很容易把“长线运营”和“让玩家每天在线更久”联系在一起，但《剑网3》团队并不这么认为。余玉贤说，真正应该留下的是有价值的内容，而不是为了填满玩家的时间而不断增加重复劳动——“你再好吃的东西，天天往人家嘴里塞，他也会吐的。”
“《剑网3》是赛季制的，”余玉贤解释道，“我只要保证你玩了这个赛季，哪怕只玩一个月、两个月，你玩得贼爽，这就够了。下个赛季，你肯定还会回来。”
团队观察到，每年《剑网3》的回流用户数量远大于新用户。有人离开一两个星期，有人离开一两个月，甚至离开三四年，最后还是会回来。离开的原因也未必是游戏不好玩，可能只是和亲友发生了矛盾，可能是被竞技场折磨得受不了，也可能只是生活里突然有了别的事情。
“可能玩家流失不是因为游戏不好玩，而是和亲友怎么怎么样了，比如说死情缘了，或者说真的是打竞技场恶心到了，”他继续说，“一旦自己的情绪过去，一想，确实是在游戏中有一点感动，就还会再回来。”
“我们也还有这么多好听的歌，是吧？”余玉贤说。
“你盯着玩家的心，你就记着初心”
■ 更新江湖的“骨架”
如果说重回50级的决定是要重新整理已经存在的江湖，那么“《剑网3》2.0”，则是在为未来重新打地基。这是本次发布会上最重磅的信息之一：《剑网3》2.0计划于2027年开放试玩。
从2017年的重制版，到2023年的旗舰版，《剑网3》已经经历过两次大规模的技术迭代。如今第三次来到技术底层，团队将与国际领先合作伙伴开展深度合作，推进底层技术、渲染表现、研发工具链和生产流程的系统升级。
余玉贤说得很直白：“这只是第一步。”团队希望借助更大的研发资源投入，“把画面质量首先拉到，市面上至少是顶流的位置”。
“下一站，接轨全球技术”
余玉贤坦率地说，《剑网3》的底层工具已经不再先进了。过去很多玩法并不是策划没有想法，而是底层工具限制了最终效果。“你们应该也感觉得出来，我们做了很多玩法，是很努力在做的，但是给你们的感觉就还差点意思。”
这次底层升级，并不是简单地让角色的发丝更飘逸、场景的光影变化更真实，而是希望重新搭建一套能够支撑未来内容生产的工具链。
余玉贤还提到，未来团队会尝试把前沿工具接入新的生产流程，并进一步改变游戏角色、甚至NPC与玩家之间的关系。
晚会中，一支串联全场的动画短片恰好把这种关系具像化了，它讲述了一名《剑网3》玩家“穿越”到游戏中，和自己的游戏角色相伴游玩的故事。随着江湖与现实一同变化，游戏角色的成长承载了玩家不少珍贵的回忆。
“从屏幕里的江湖，到屏幕外的人间”
而《剑网3》的江湖，也正在慢慢延伸至屏幕之外。
今年《剑网3》全新资料片将携手山西省古建筑与彩塑壁画保护研究院，通过数字技术复刻悬空寺，并以有爱玩家的名义，向山西省文物保护基金管理中心进行捐赠，支持山西古建保护与修缮。古建合作其实并不是一开始就规划好的“IP战略”，余玉贤解释，《剑网3》做的是一个尽可能还原历史的武侠世界，当游戏里的角色走到西安、走到大雁塔，就需要面对真实存在的历史。
于是，他们向真正了解这些建筑和历史的人寻求合作。“到了西安是不是要做大雁塔？一做大雁塔，是不是就得还原得更好一点？”
除此之外，《剑网3》还公布了与《凡人修仙传》、《道诡异仙》、《风云》等多个IP联动的计划。随着这些IP的名字一一出现，现场爆发出一阵阵欢呼声，正应了余玉贤对于团队选择联动IP的判断标准的说法：“很简单，就是要玩家喜欢。”
■ “谨祝诸君武运昌吉”
值得一提的是，这次晚会充分运用了场馆的优势，做了不少有趣的舞美设计。甚至在发布会环节中，除了随着介绍内容切换画面的四面大屏幕，制作人脚下的舞台也在不断变化着图案。
制作人结束介绍走下台，灯光很快暗了下来，舞台换了一种颜色。古风歌手们陆续登台，龚琳娜也再次出现在台上——她已经是《剑网3》的老朋友，玩家甚至会开玩笑说，团队要“牢牢抓住龚琳娜老师”——熟悉的角色、故事和声音重新出现在大屏幕上。
龚琳娜演唱《万象长安》
玩家们经常说周年庆晚会是“大型KTV”现场。来之前，我的剑纯亲友还特地提醒我，最好提前练练几首歌，“不然到了现场，大家都会唱”。还有好心玩家在社媒分享歌词PDF文件，我也下载了一份。
事实证明，“大型KTV”这个说法并不夸张。熟悉的旋律一首接一首响起，《九万里》、《大美江湖》……大屏幕上的画面跟着音乐切换，观众手中的荧光棒变幻着色彩，甚至组成了游过观众席的鲲鹏，1.8万人的大合唱很快把整个场馆填满。
也许对于很多玩家来说，这些歌曲早就不只是简单的游戏音乐了——在这个已经存在了十七年的江湖，玩家的游戏生涯早已和现实缠绕在了一起。一个角色的培养可能对应一段学生时代，一个帮会的名字也许意味着那些珍贵的友谊，一件已经不再重要的装备，也会让人想起当初一起刷过很多遍副本的那些人，想起后来的各奔东西……游戏里的时间没有停止，但很多侠士的生活已经向前走了很远。
幸运的是，江湖也没有停下脚步。
晚会快结束时，观众席里有人喊：“《剑网3》四十七周年快乐！”
——2025年，《剑网3》曾提出“还要再战30年”，如今站在17周年的这个节点往前望去，让这个江湖再活几十年的目标，其实也并不算遥不可及。

title: 为了在游戏行业“上岸”，首先要准备两年
text:
■ 秋招提前开始了
7月中旬，小周刚开启暑期实习不到两周，突然发现：他关注的几家游戏公司的2027届秋招提前批开了。
“提前批”即秋招前奏，大厂为抢占优质生源提前开启的招聘，与之对应的招聘程序也会做一些简化。不过对于小周来说，提前批比预想中得早了很多。
米哈游的提前批和正式批，毕业生只能投递一次
小周是2027届毕业生，想要找一份游戏客户端开发的工作。暑期实习刚刚开始，他的简历还没有更新。与此同时，他还发现：“只有鹰角和莉莉丝才是‘真正的’提前批，因为有第二次投递机会，有‘复活甲’。”而米哈游的提前批则会与正式批会共享投递次数，“投了就没了”。
但时间不等人，提前批一般在7月底截止。小周将实习内容丢给AI润色，硬着头皮向鹰角和莉莉丝投递了简历。从7月提前批开启，这场秋招将持续到10月底，他把心仪的企业列入电子表格，打算等到8月丰富简历后再逐一投递。
小周向触乐解释：“校招为滚动录取，大家觉得七八月是名校毕业生和大厂实习生的天下，所以，等8月底和9月初再进入新的'池子'，会更有机会。”
但到了9月初，大家又会担心岗位是否会提前满额、停止录用。“这就需要取舍。”小周说。
■ 节奏不同的秋招图景
校招提前开启，并不是每位应届毕业生都能回过神来，但几乎所有人都有一个共识，“那就是一定要抓住秋招”。企业招聘名额有限。大部分毕业生都认为，秋招会开放大部分岗位，春招负责补录，机会将会减少很多。
2026届全国高校毕业生数字再破新高
8月中下旬，小周结束了腾讯实习。他已经陆续投递了8份简历，开始收获秋招面试机会。
上周，他参加了鹰角提前批的一面。因为过于紧张，小周回答得“支离破碎”。但他又自我宽慰：“即使面得好也进不去，听说去年鹰角的游戏客户端开发岗只招一个人，这怎么争呢？肯定还有更厉害的清华、上海交大的毕业生。”
面试过程中，小周发现，如何与AI沟通，成为了今年秋招面试绕不开的话题。小周觉得，要回答“如何与AI协作”不难，平时在学校搞科研、做实验都会与AI沟通、用AI写代码。他苦恼的是要控制表情，不能“眼神乱瞟”，否则容易被认定为“AI作弊”。
并且，回答还要够快。有次，小周思考一番后才给出答案，当即受到面试官质疑：“你是不是用AI了？”小周急忙将摄像头环绕一圈自证清白：“你看，什么都没有。”说起这事时，他还有些庆幸：“直接问我还能自证，如果面试官写下疑似AI作弊，100%过不了。”除此之外，面对棘手的场景题、手撕（手写代码）题，小周只能一边面试，一边学习，期待靠“局外养成”让下次面试可以更加游刃有余。
给豆包打电话，面试时将手机放于面前
过去两周，秋秋也在参加面试。她在上海一所高校内读英语笔译方向的专硕，正在找一份游戏运营与营销的工作，但她想要找的是一个实习岗位。她计划在垂直领域继续积累经验，再在秋招换取一份心仪Offer。
在此之前，秋秋参加了多次实习岗位面试，但均以失败告终。在面试过程中，秋秋最苦恼的问题是，“一款游戏的海内外用户有何区别？”每次她都感觉自己没答到点子上。她也找人请教，但一直没找到满意的标准答案。后来她认为，如果要做海外相关的业务，还是得去长期深入海外的游戏社区去观察。
更让她纠结的是，实习与秋招会互相耽误进度。她要准备实习面试，就顾不上秋招，但如果错过，损失会很大。被身边人劝说后，秋秋决定先参加秋招。但浏览了一圈，她最想去的两家公司根本没有放出适合她的营销和运营岗位。对于这种情况，一名游戏行业HR对触乐说，营销及运营岗位取决于项目需求，数量与释放时间不固定。
秋秋想去的深蓝互动只放出了日本市场营销策划
油画专业的芽芽还未参加秋招面试，她仍在准备角色设计作品集。考研失败后，她决定延毕一年，保留应届生身份参加秋招，应聘一份游戏角色原画工作。
这个决定，在将考公视为正道的山东近乎为“下坡路”。芽芽回忆：“学校没有这样的案例，同学不理解，领导还找我开会，阵仗挺大，最后他们才尊重我的选择。”确定延毕后，她在网上四处打听，经人介绍找了一位颇受好评的原画老师。到了今年8月底，她已学习原画两月有余。
但秋招开始，她又免不了焦虑。“我害怕错过每个机会。但也不敢多想，只有赶紧准备作品集，现在能力还不够。”为了能够睡着，芽芽一直在吃安眠药助眠。从考研开始，失眠就顺着挥之不去的压力找上了她。
■ 要尽早开跑
游戏企业的秋招会持续一个季度，学生却已经至少筹备了两年。小周在研一开始思考自己的未来方向，他觉得自己考虑得已经算晚的了。
小周在2024年入学，修读网络空间安全（车联网方向）。他选择游戏行业的原因比较现实——大学就读的实验室并非国内最顶尖的一批，车联网市场的岗位需求量也不高，加上自己平时爱玩游戏，几番考虑后，小周选择了游戏客户端开发。
为了尽快入行，小周参加过两次腾讯游戏的“开局一课”。这门课堂由腾讯在2025年开启，分为策划、美术等四个方向，主要面向大学生提供职业入门培训。
课程每周开设两节。老师通常是腾讯员工，小周感觉，“有时像是抓了一名加班的程序员（来上课）。”课程内容较为基础，“教你把引擎安好，后面的基本就不管了”。由于这门启蒙课程主讲UE，小周后续就选择了自己专攻的游戏引擎。
腾讯游戏开局一课也有应聘加成
最初，小周觉得游戏开发分外有趣。他很喜欢游戏开发引擎“所见即所得”带来的正反馈——写入代码与逻辑，点击运行，游戏界面就会显示出来。他还会观看游戏开发组的幕后采访视频，看大家分享如何设计角色，感觉他们彼此志趣相投。但小周又转念一想：“似乎程序员的身影没有出现过，或许他们和这种氛围无关。”
在进一步了解游戏开发后，越玩游戏，小周越觉得自己前途渺茫，想着“他们能写出这么厉害的东西”。而他写的东西有时候都不能运行。
2025年暑期开始，他花半年用UE做出一款第三人称FPS的Demo，将“走动逻辑”“碰撞”“网络同步”都写了一遍。小周跟着网络教程学习，碰见问题再去查。小周解释：“这也是写得这么慢的原因，但挨个看课程，百分百来不及了。”他也在这时候调整了自己的心态，“别整天想着学一小会就可以进入什么公司，只有努力去写，闷头去写”。
对小周来说，决定开始游戏行业求职后，所有的时间都变得非常紧张。实验室的工作并不轻松，发表论文数量也有硬性指标。“导师对我的要求更高，秋招回去就得准备毕业论文了。”小周说。
为了找到一份好工作，高校学生都在提早做准备。相较而言，他们发现，学校的老教师对严峻的就业形势不甚了解，年轻的老师有所耳闻，但又不能感同身受。近些年，能为教育系统带来变量的是AI。
秋秋研究的英语笔译方向受AI影响很深。老师在课堂上会讲到“AI赋能”，但她觉得翻译行业已经发生了翻天覆地的变化。“现在没有翻译工作不需要AI了，都是人机协同。”在秋秋看来，AI的翻译能力已经越来越成熟。
近年来，国内部分高校取消外语类专业本科生、研究生招生
但英语专业的毕业生去向相对固定，秋秋说，同专业同学大多会去高校、出版社实习，正式工作会考虑考公，去制造业类的硬件厂商。秋秋也曾去事业单位参加实习，但她觉得工作氛围有些古板。相较而言，她更喜欢游戏行业。
专硕学习时长只有两年，时间更为紧迫。她在研一时刷到了一些帖子。“要找到好的正式工作，一个人至少要有两三段实习。”秋秋算了一下，“寒假就得实习了。”
■ 实习要垂直
为了找到一份游戏运营工作，秋秋曾斥资8000元在网上报了相关课程。一共10节课，老师会布置作业，让学生拆解游戏，并会负责无限次修改。这份作业也能成为学员用于面试的作品集，老师还能帮忙面试复盘——整体听起来很美好。
但等到找实习，秋秋才发现，这门游戏运营课程没有太大帮助。因为，她没有一份足够垂直的游戏行业实习经历。
在应届生眼中，找实习如同肉鸽游戏中的“爬塔”。你要获得一份好的实习，首先要有一份实习。“怎么样才能有鹰角和莉莉丝实习？你有腾讯和网易的实习就可以了。”小周说，这是计算机领域的笑话。不少应届生还会十分看重毕业前的暑期实习。如果能够获得转正机会，他们也就比参加秋招的同学更早拿到正职Offer。
从2026年1月起，秋秋做过两份实习。第一份做了两月，工作内容是网络小说的出海运营。接着，她又找了一份电竞赛事社群运营的工作。
这份电竞赛事运营工作持续了5个月，秋秋主要负责电竞赛事频道的选题策划与运营。团队人手紧缺，在长达3月的比赛期，她几乎连轴转，像一个随时应答的机器：“只要醒着就得回复消息”。
有时比赛会从下午5点持续到午夜。视频制作具有滞后性，她需要提前回寝室，再工作至凌晨一两点。学校还有课程，她因此牺牲了学习时间。除了周三上午和周四，她都会去公司报到。有时上课时，即使坐在课桌前，她都会在下面处理工作。
“就是忙到了这个地步。”秋秋说。
虽然有机会转正，今年8月，秋秋还是选择了离职。这份工作与游戏运营相去甚远，她的身体也吃不消，并且，“一万出头的月薪”在上海不算高，仅够勉强维持生活。
另一边，小周的实习经历也有些曲折。为了在2026年暑期找到实习，他从3月开始投递简历，投了15-16家知名的企业。虽然学历过关，但简历没有通过不少厂商的初筛。经过一番折腾，最后他还是拿到了4份Offer。他认为这是“面试资源的差异”。大厂更愿意给机会。
应届生简历被挂是常态
去腾讯报到后，他又发现了自己与他人的差距。其他人是科班出身，他是“野路子”。这是他的第一份实习，有同事从大二就开始实习了。工作内容比较基础。实习生负责报表数据的整理、产品的“热更新”，只用Lua代码，更新引擎上的“脚手架”，不会直接接触引擎底层。
小周也能理解，实习生就待两三个月，也不一定能留任，正职费劲教也是白费力气。但这样，实习生又会面临没有产出的境况，忙于无法更新在简历上的工作。
“在我们计算机的实习圈子，如果遇到这种情况，大家会考虑仔细去看项目组的文档和代码，自己学习，思考可以说自己参与实现了哪个模块的代码。”小周说，这也是没有办法的办法。
他在实习之前，就知道没有机会转正。组内HC不多，名额还要按项目分。不是所有项目都能蒸蒸日上，有次，他路过了隔壁项目组的楼层，里面“太压抑了”，他都不敢往里看。不过，好在大厂实习的经历至少能为简历镀金。
■ 还有退路吗？
他们怀抱兴趣，想要进入游戏行业，依据网络信息和身边人的讲述，逐步构建起心中游戏行业的面貌，这时，他们开始认为，游戏行业或许不是唯一解。
2027届毕业生规划毕业后去处时，会考量更多现实情况。小周心里有张排序表，他是米哈游游戏的玩家，排在首位的是米哈游，所谓“有米选米”，其次是鹰角与莉莉丝，然后是腾讯、网易和深蓝互动，接着是其他叫得上名的大公司。他看重公司是否有产品、现金流是否稳定，“毕竟现在项目很容易死掉”。
2026届毕业生看重的要素
不同的项目情况也会在求职者之间流传。经过面试，在各种课程群、招聘群里和其他毕业生交流，小周会很容易知道哪家公司在预研什么项目，更偏好什么人才。虽然眼下学习Unity会更好找工作，但他相信自己选择的UE引擎将成为未来的趋势。
不少客户端开发岗位开始聚焦UE5开发引擎
有时，小周也会想，如果工作压力太大，实在不行就在二线城市的国企银行找份工作。作为程序员，他会考虑职业寿命，认为不能将纸面工资当工资。小周说：“就算一个月拿4万，研究生毕业后做了5年，到30岁被辞退，月薪4万也不多。”不过，小周听在银行科技岗工作的学姐说，今年办公室内来了两名清华、北大的新人，他感觉竞争压力也不小。
对于文科专业与艺术专业，考公考编考研仍是比较热门的传统选择。据国家公务员局公布的数据，2026年国考报名人数为371.8万人，另据教育部统计，2026年全国硕士研究生招生考试报名人数为 343 万。
此外，AI岗位也成为一股新兴趋势，竞争也十分激烈。小周与秋秋都听说有朋友去了AI岗位。秋秋的朋友在2026年将AI产品作为求职方向，在五一长假学习AI，找到了一份实习，目前正在准备暑期转正答辩，三个人竞争一个岗位。
而小周非常坚定地拒绝AI岗位。虽然现在开发已经离不开AI，他甚至听说网易有AI代码比例的硬性指标。但他对新风口、新兴岗位一向警惕。“万一明年不火了怎么办？我的秋招只有一次，赌不起。”小周说。
与小周的想法一样，秋秋也不准备在游戏行业吊死。她觉得运营工作本身没有门槛，但现在太卷了，所以门槛提了上去。运营社群时，她也时常感觉自己的灵感趋于枯竭。思考后路时，她觉得短视频、电商也不是不可以，只是想到要放弃两段实习经历，有些可惜。
对于芽芽来说，她没有了退路。于她而言，考研原本就是一个逃避现实的选项。她觉得赚钱有趣，在大学，她做过模特、家教，也在米画师接稿，一张头像的单价在千元左右，但她也更加看重稳定。她原本想继续读研，先读和游戏相关的数字媒体艺术，再多给自己一些时间考虑。但现在不能再逃避了。
她考虑过考公，但美术专业只能选择“三不限”（不限专业、不限户籍等）的岗位，竞争激烈。考研失败后，她认为自己的天赋点不在文化课上，她想靠绘画挣钱。她将自己的作品集私信发给游戏业界大佬，对方认为她有潜力，鼓励她延毕准备校招，找一份好的工作。
但这个抉择过程令她精神备受折磨。犹豫了三月，决定延毕后，芽芽反而心里松了一口气。“今年经历太多，（秋招）已经不算事了。”她觉得最焦虑的时间点已经过去，想着：“付出这么大的代价，一定要找到一份好的工作。”
不过她也不确定这个决定是否一定正确。她想起，自己曾在学校门口遇见一名卖烤冷面的小贩，聊起来才知道对方曾经是游戏厂商的原画外包，年薪三四十万。“干原画太累了。”对方对她说，“熬夜到九、十点是常态，说是双休，但从来没双休过。”
芽芽还是决定往前走，尽管在油画专业，她身边毕业后选择进入互联网的人不多，“去年有学长秋招进了游戏行业，他是我身边第一个进入这个行业的人，他给了我信心。”
目前，让她有些焦虑的是AI。虽然秋招原画岗大多要求AI能力，但授课老师禁止学生练习时用AI跑图。芽芽也曾依赖AI绘图，反而退步了。现在，她改掉了这个习惯，摸索如何界定AI的边界。
秋招原画岗大多需要AI能力
画了一批原画后，老师告诉她可以投递秋招了，但她准备再丰富一下作品集的风格，增加胜算。“对于小白来说，原画岗位不看实习，只看作品集和个人能力。”芽芽说。在她的计划中，薪资最为优先，其次才是项目与城市。不过，她认为首先要有份工作。“不是我挑工作，是工作挑我。”
■ 结语
据前程无忧发布的《2026校园招聘白皮书》，校招时间整体前移，提前批成为不少企业的选择。而据教育部统计，2026年，全国高校毕业生规模预计1270万，比去年多了48万。为了能够找到一份好工作，他们都在与时间赛跑，争取跑得比其他人更快。
对于想要进入游戏行业的应届毕业生，他们认为找工作如“爬塔”，拥有几份好的实习经历，就有机会换取一份好的工作Offer。但等到真正参加秋招后，他们才发现一个悖论：如果AI的发展正在让岗位数量缩减，那么他们提前准备实习、Demo和作品集，越往上爬，选择机会也没有因此增多。
一名95后从业者对触乐感叹：“现在招聘的小孩比我们当时优秀太多，不论是学历、经验和思维方法都很厉害，但是他们现在100个人只能进1个，我们当时100个人可能可以进来25个。”
目前，小周仍在等待新的面试，小周觉得自己一定能找到工作，只是不确定能否找到一份好的工作。
秋秋已经开始向秋招岗位投递简历。她花两元买了一份秋招岗位表格，准备从上往下投。如果没有进展，两周后，她将继续寻找实习机会。她偶尔会翻翻手机里的相片。今年8月，她去欧洲旅游，站在萨尔茨堡的沃尔夫冈湖边，山与湖景非常开阔。她想着：“天地这么大，为何要为了眼前的这些小事烦忧。”
秋秋很喜欢的一片湖景
不过旅游回来后，她还是在秋招前去了趟上海的龙华寺，祈祷找到一份好工作。她听说，龙华寺在事业运上十分灵验。她之前实习认识的前同事也一同前去，希望换一份新的工作。
芽芽决定在9月正式参加秋招。在他们的预想中，理想情况是在11月找到一份工作，这样，他们就能早点上岸。而芽芽觉得，或许在找到工作后，她就能安心睡着了。

title: 触乐怪话：也不知道《GTA 6》的音乐要花多少钱
text:
触乐怪话，每天胡侃和游戏有关的屁事、鬼事、新鲜事。
这是个需要严肃考虑的问题（图/小罗）
上周五，受祝老师启发，我从预告片选曲的角度，写了一篇分析《GTA 6》故事走向的稿子。其实一开始，我们只想简单介绍这次预告里使用的歌曲，及其文化背景，大概会是一篇很快速的文章。但当我把R星在这次预告里用到的歌曲扒下来，放在一起时，我发现这份歌单的作用远比我想得要更重要。
这是一次影视级别的配乐运用。开场用3首南方说唱交代事情的地理和文化背景；男女主角分头行动的时候，分别用男声演唱和女声演唱的2首歌来讲述两位各自的人生状态；用Depeche Mode的《People Are People》和Prefab Sprout的《Cars and Girls》来暗示故事的主题。几乎没有哪首歌单纯只是作为氛围烘托出现的——具体的分析我写在那篇稿子里了，这里就不再重复展开了。
R星的音乐审美已经在过往的“GTA”系列里得到过证明，他们能做到这种程度，我不意外。但最让我感慨的一点在于，美国流行文化里有这么多适合的素材供创作者选择。
我在那篇文章里也提到，《GTA 6》有意地将这次的音乐核心主题聚焦在合成器流行，尤其是80年代的作品。他们这次的主题曲和视觉风格也是，但更加现代。所以，R星的音乐总监在挑选歌曲的时候，不仅要考虑作品内容，还要考虑作品风格。在这样的限制下，他们依然能找到《People Are People》和《Cars and Girls》这种作品风格、知名度以及主题表达近乎完美契合的歌。我是真的佩服。
同时，我也很羡慕。因为换个角度想，假如一家中国游戏公司要做一款类似的游戏，他们的音乐总监面临同样的选曲工作，他能选择的作品有多少？唉，忽然想到，这不就是《无限大》吗。同样是前几天发了定档预告的《无限大》，也选了一首在我们自己流行文化里留下印记的作品，王菲的《梦中人》——我个人觉得是王菲的版本，不过因为没有听到歌词部分，也有可能是这首歌的原唱爱尔兰乐队The Cranberries的《Dreams》，甚至是制作组重新找了翻唱。
但无论怎么说，国内的游戏制作组在选曲方面遇到的难度要比R星大得多，比较后者能选择的空间远大于我们。就是挺尴尬，也很复杂。所谓的“流行文化”原本就是一个舶来概念，以流行音乐为例，我们在这个框架下构建的作品也不过几十年的时间，无论是广度还是深度都不够。而且很多时候，流行文化作品要成为能被引用的经典，更需要在传播和讨论中才能形成它在大众层面的“意义”，不然很难形成共鸣——就像最近爆红的《牛来》......哎呀，这话题怎么越扯越远了。
还是回到《GTA 6》的选曲上来。
前两年我还在音乐行业工作的时候，有件事引发了大范围的讨论。当时是Heaven 17乐队的主创，在社交媒体发帖，说自己收到了一份来自R星的授权申请，后者希望在《GTA 6》中使用乐队的歌曲《Temptation》。一开始这位音乐人还很激动，觉得是一个“挣大钱”的机会，但当他翻到offer的具体条款时，气坏了：7500美元，一次性买断，永久在游戏中使用。“Go fuck yourself。”他在帖子里直言不讳。
Heaven 17乐队主创吐槽帖，够尖锐
Heaven 17也是一支成名于80年代的合成器流行乐队，而这首歌是他们最热门的作品。尽管7500美元的报价是这位主创分到的价格，R星给这首歌的三位创作者一共开出的报价是22500美元。但依据这首歌的知名度和如今流媒体的播放量，从歌曲授权的角度，这份报价确实低得出人意料，尤其考虑到这是《GTA6》。
这件事引发了对于音乐定价的讨论。也许有人会觉得作品被用于《GTA 6》这样级别的游戏是一种“荣幸”，会带来许多金钱之外的收益。但对于一些创作者来说，有些东西比钱更重要。
话又说回来，我们不妨算一笔账。据统计，2013年《GTA 5》首发版本使用的授权歌曲大概240首。如果按Heaven 17透露的价格算，一首歌22500美元。要注意，这是给音乐人的钱，算上唱片公司的分成，通常是双方各50%，那一首歌的授权费用是4.5万美元。2013年《GTA 5》原版发布时，一共有约240首授权歌曲，这样算下来授权费大概为1000万美元，而在2014年增强版发布时，游戏里收录的歌曲总数超过了400首，那授权费用会接近2000万美元。有这笔钱都够《33号远征队》开发两次了。
《GTA 5》的音乐总监Ivan Pavlovich在接受英国卫报采访时透露，当时他们一共接触过1500首歌的授权，最终谈成合作的数量只有四分之一。而且，你要是听过游戏里的电台便知道，虽然出现的知名音乐人很多，但大部分也不是他们最有名的作品。
《GTA 5》的故事设置在以洛杉矶为原型的洛圣都，美国西海岸。游戏电台里也有一个叫做“West Coast Classics”的电台，其中出现的西海岸说唱歌曲还是缺少相当多的“经典”。若要补齐的话，得多花不少钱。
所以，再把授权费用的因素纳入考量，从音乐选曲角度分析《GTA 6》，我会觉得是在看一件“文化奇观”。

title: 《流放之路2》制作人：我们已经准备好进入1.0了
text:
《流放之路》（Path of Exile）由新西兰工作室Grinding Gear Games（下文简称GGG）开发，是一款很难用几句话解释清楚的ARPG。
2013年正式上线后，它靠丰富的Build体系、庞大的天赋树、赛季制内容和玩家主导的交易与攻略生态运营了十余年。对不少老玩家来说，它的魅力恰恰来自那些需要花时间研究的系统：一个技能、一件装备或者一次天赋调整，都可能让玩家重新思考自己的Build。
2016年，腾讯代理了《流放之路》系列的一代产品，正式引进国服。2018年，腾讯完成了对GGG的主要股份收购，达成控股。在得到腾讯囊括开发、运营、资源调度等维度的全方面支持后，2024年12月，GGG新一代的野心之作《流放之路2》开启Early Access。
作为时隔十余年的正统续作，它并没有简单地把前作的内容搬到新游戏里，而是进行了大量重新设计。原本，开发团队预计抢先体验开始后大约6个月就能完成剩余内容，但实际开发远比预想复杂。直到今年科隆游戏展，GGG才公布《流放之路2》将于2026年12月11日正式进入1.0版本。
《流放之路2》的国服版本《流放之路：降临》于2025年9月推出，此后，国服团队和GGG共同推进了交易市集优化等全球玩家均可享用的便利迭代，一些国服独有的优化调整也引发了全球玩家的关注。0.5.0版本前后，中国服公告曾公布针对多人组队掉落的调整，而这一改动并未出现在当时的全球版本公告中，也引发了国际玩家社区的讨论。
因此，《流放之路2》这款3A品质的刷宝大作现在面对的已经不只是“什么时候正式发布”的问题：一款经过长期Early Access、持续根据玩家反馈调整的ARPG，究竟要做到什么程度，才算真正准备好进入1.0？而来自不同地区的玩家反馈，又会在多大程度上影响最终的游戏设计？
在今年科隆游戏展期间，我们和《流放之路2》制作人Jonathan Rogers（下文简称Jonathan）聊了聊。他谈到了0.5.0之后的Endgame、1.0需要达到的标准、《流放之路2》与前作之间的差异，以及中国玩家和全球版本之间的关系。
《流放之路2》制作人Jonathan Rogers
■ 1.0之前需要解决什么问题
问 ：经历了这么长时间的测试后，你现在会如何形容游戏的核心玩法循环和主要乐趣？与最初的构想相比，哪些部分发生了最大的变化？
Jonathan ：我觉得与其说是构想发生了变化，不如说有太多事情是我们必须努力做好的——这花了很长时间。终局玩法就是一个很好的例子。我们原本以为自己知道怎样把它做好，因为《流放之路》（一代）的终局玩法很出色，也受到很多玩家喜爱。但把异界图鉴改成无限延伸之后，游戏的整体体验发生了非常明显的变化，所以我们不得不回过头来，大幅调整许多内容。
最近的0.5.0更新上线后，玩家似乎都认同现在的终局玩法已经非常出色。事实上，很多人甚至比起《流放之路》（一代）更喜欢现在的终局玩法。这正是我们在进入正式发布之前必须做好的事情之一。
刚开始抢先体验时，我们以为大约六个月就能完成游戏。但实际上，由于相较《流放之路》（一代）发生了太多变化，要把所有事情都做到位花了更长时间。这就是整个过程如此漫长的原因。
问 ：从抢先体验到1.0，你认为游戏经历的最重要变化是什么？
Jonathan ：我刚才提到的终局玩法改动非常重要。除此之外，还有一些影响很大的变化，比如“疾跑”（Sprint）。另一个尤其重要的变化是新的交易系统。交易对很多玩家来说都极为关键；与过去相比，现在能够直接在游戏内与其他玩家交易，是一项非常重大的改变。
此外，还有无数琐碎的平衡调整和持续改进，累积起来也带来了巨大改变。如果把0.1.0版本和现在的游戏进行比较，我认为仅凭这些不断积累的变化，玩家体验就已经能提升很多了。
问 ：如果要选出几项最能代表“游戏现在已经准备好进入1.0”的改动，会是什么？
Jonathan ：在1.0版本上线之前，有几件事情必须做得足够好。首先，我们需要完成整个故事，这显然是必不可少的。其次，我们也必须证明终局玩法对玩家来说确实足够好。最初这一点做得并不好，因此我们进行了大幅改进；现在，我们相信终局玩法已经非常出色。
我们还必须尽可能把物品系统做好，而要把它调整到位是经历了好几轮迭代的。最后，我们需要让游戏平衡达到更理想的状态。这一直非常具有挑战性，但每一轮迭代都让它变得更好。
我们原本预计抢先体验阶段的玩家不会那么多，也以为可以在大多数人开始游玩前完成其中一些改动。但由于实际玩家数量非常庞大，某些平衡调整反而变得更难进行。即便如此，我们仍在持续做必要的改动，每次推出新版本，构筑多样性——也就是玩家实际采用的不同流派数量——都在继续增加。我认为方向是正确的，只是把这些事情全部做好确实需要大量时间。
问 ：1.0版本是否意味着团队已经完成了最初对《流放之路2》的全部设想？最终成品与最开始预想的方向有什么不同？未来的更新会专注于哪些方向？
Jonathan ：我们原本想交付的内容与实际将要交付的内容之间，唯一的差别是我们曾计划准备好全部12个职业。正式发布时不会有完整的12个职业。除此之外，我们承诺的其他内容全部都已实现：包含所有章节的完整主线、远超过100场的Boss战、超过600种怪物、超过100个主线区域，以及全部终局内容。坦率地说，我认为我们在终局内容上甚至是超额交付。游戏的规模非常庞大，绝对达到了我对1.0版本的期待。
差别只在职业数量，但即使如此，我们上线时拥有的职业也会比大多数游戏更多——更不用说还有各个升华职业——所以我并不太担心。真正困难的是，抢先体验刚开始时，我们对迈向1.0究竟需要做多少工作想得过于天真。这个过程中我们学到了很多。尽管以前已经发布过一款游戏，也以为自己很清楚该怎么做，但真正再制作一款新游戏时，人很容易忘记，要让整个游戏运转起来，需要叠加多少层额外内容。
最大的挑战，是意识到我们究竟需要多少终局内容，才能与《流放之路》（一代）竞争。当年一代发布时，并没有另一款《流放之路》与它竞争。如今二代面对的竞争对手正是我们自己的第一代，而且这个对手非常强大，所以我们必须制作海量内容，才能让二代站得住脚。
《流放之路2》科隆展台试玩区
■ 在续作中重新学习
问 ：从《流放之路》（一代）到《流放之路2》，有没有哪些过去十多年已经被证明有效、但不再适合今天ARPG玩家的设计原则？
Jonathan ：最主要的一点是，《流放之路》（一代）刚推出时，玩家对复杂系统的接受度甚至比现在更高。就可构筑的流派数量而言，我们依然是一款非常复杂的游戏，但我们必须触达更广泛的市场，也必须让更多的玩家更容易上手。
这并不意味着游戏会彻底走向轻度化。我们仍然保留了庞大的天赋树以及许多有深度的系统，但与此同时，《流放之路2》比《流放之路》（一代）容易上手非常多，而且没有因此牺牲深度。自第一代游戏推出以来，玩家对交易的期待也发生了显著变化，这同样是我们必须应对的问题。我认为，复杂度和交易是两个最主要的方面。
归根结底，这两点都源于整个游戏行业对用户体验的要求不断提高。动画品质乃至方方面面，都必须达到更高的标准。相比之下，《流放之路》（一代）如今显得陈旧得多。今天再制作这样的游戏，就必须具备一定水准的动作游戏表现。我认为，我们很大胆地重新定义了一款ARPG在动作性方面必须做到什么。其他ARPG能否在这方面与我们竞争，会是一件很有意思的事；就目前的成果而言，我们相当有信心。
问 ：这次Gamescom公布了新的内容。除了单纯增加更多可玩内容之外，你们希望它解决《流放之路2》目前存在的哪些问题？
Jonathan ：我们最近已经处理了终局玩法方面的问题，我认为现在的表现好得多。仍然需要改善的一个领域是传奇物品。我们还计划了大量相关内容，会在ExileCon上公布。抢先体验初期制作的传奇物品，远没有今天推出的这些好。目前仍有许多早期设计达不到我们现在的标准，因此必须更新并加强它们，同时还要制作大量新的传奇物品。到了1.0版本，传奇物品应该会好得多。
另一个领域是游戏平衡。我们一直在迭代和改善，但永远还有更多事情要做；这是一项没有终点的工作。辅助宝石尤其需要大量改进，因此它们是当前平衡工作的重点。我们希望让更多辅助宝石具备实用价值，移除那些我们认为没有用的，同时增加更多真正有用的宝石。这也是我们希望持续改进的方面。
这些是比较主要的问题。其他方面我大体满意，不过仍有一些较小的问题。一个明显的例子是塞赫玛试炼，也就是类似圣所玩法的试炼。目前，两种升华试炼都还不够好。其中一种很快就会迎来重大改进，另一种也需要为1.0版本解决。
最后，主线剧情中的某些区域仍然缺少必要内容，还没有达到我们期望的完成度。有些原本计划制作的内容最终没有完成，因此我们必须确保把这些缺失部分全部补齐。
问 ：1.0版本这个时间点，比你们最初预期的更早还是更晚？
Jonathan ：它肯定比我在0.1.0版本发布时预计的晚得多。我们当时以为大约六个月就能完成游戏的其余部分，结果却花了两年。因此，它比预期晚了很多，不过我觉得这是游戏行业里的常态了。
问 ：是什么让你们确信，游戏现在已经准备好进入正式发布阶段？
Jonathan ：对我来说，是0.5.0版本让玩家真正喜欢上了终局玩法。只有当游戏具备可重复游玩的价值——也就是玩家愿意一遍又一遍地玩——我们才算准备好进入1.0。因此，看到终局玩法现在变得更加有趣，是一个非常重要的信号。
此外，即使仍处于抢先体验阶段，玩家规模也在增长。这意味着正式发布后很可能还会继续增长，也让我们相当有信心。
“永火之咒”齐拉克的宝库
■ 从一代到二代
问 ：对于长期运营的ARPG来说，大型更新往往也会吸引老玩家回归。在设计这次更新时，你们如何平衡“吸引回归玩家”和“真正改变整体游戏体验”这两个目标？
Jonathan ：我们现在有两款游戏：《流放之路》（一代）和《流放之路2》，它们的设计目标差异很大。对《流放之路》（一代）来说，我们已经不再特别担心吸引新玩家，主要目标是让现有玩家都感到满意。每当《流放之路》（一代）推出新版本，玩家数量都足以与3A大作相媲美。当然，我们总希望做得更好，但现在《流放之路》（一代）的重点主要是为现有玩家提供他们想要的内容。
另一方面，《流放之路2》则在努力让内容更容易被新玩家接受，这是一个重要目标。这个过程中确实存在一些小矛盾，因为《流放之路》（一代）的玩家不一定喜欢我们所做的每项改动，但我相信，我们是有可能同时吸引这两批人的。
我认为0.5.0版本已经证明了这一点。越来越多《流放之路》（一代）的玩家开始喜欢《流放之路2》，我也越来越常听到一些极其忠实的一代玩家说，他们觉得二代或许正开始变得比一代更好。当然，我一直认为二代更好，但现在我也从越来越多其他人口中听到这种评价。因此，我认为《流放之路2》完全可以成为一款让这些玩家也乐在其中的游戏。即便如此，两款游戏的根本设计目标依然不同：一款几乎完全面向现有用户，另一款则还需要触达新玩家。
问 ：《流放之路》系列高度依赖玩家社区研究构筑、制作攻略并分享知识。随着1.0版本吸引更多新玩家，你如何看待社区知识在整体体验中的作用？你们怎样判断哪些信息应该由游戏直接说明，哪些仍应留给社区自行发现？
Jonathan ：坦率地说，这非常难。决定哪些内容应该公开、哪些应该留给玩家自己发现时，显然把一切都公布出来会带来营销收益，但玩家也喜欢保留一些能够亲自探索和发现的东西。
实际上，我们发现多公布一些内容通常效果更好。很多玩家最终并不会知道我们公布的每一件事，因为并非所有人都会关注公告。因此，我们往往会在公告里谈论相当多的内容。
倾听社区、理解大家真正想要什么，也是我工作中非常重要的一部分。我会密切关注社区，努力理解玩家的想法，不过随着受众扩大，这件事也越来越困难。即使是聚集在同一个社区里的一群人，彼此的观点也可能截然不同。随着我们进入更多地区、面对更多语言，这项工作变得更具挑战，因为不同地区对游戏应该如何设计，可能有完全不同的看法。我们只能尽力持续跟进所有这些意见，并做到最好。
精灵Aoife正在寻找能帮助她的勇士
■ 中国玩家和全球版本
问 ：从制作组的视角来看，中国玩家和其他地区玩家在游玩方式上有哪些明显差异？
Jonathan ：我通常会尽量以同样的方式看待所有玩家。在我看来，各地玩家想要的东西都非常相似：他们希望感到自己很强大，希望游戏体验足够好，等等。就这一点而言，我并不认为中国玩家与世界其他地区的玩家存在根本差异。
当然，中国市场有自身的情况，尤其体现在玩家愿意接受怎样的游戏产品上。我要说的是，中国玩家对游戏的期待非常高。我对此没有意见，但这确实是一个非常明显的特点，而要满足这些期待可能相当困难。我们必须迎接这项挑战，并竭尽所能。
《流放之路：降临》国服转免定档12月18日

title: 科技巨头的游戏败局：亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌为何玩不转游戏业务？
text:
科技巨头的游戏败局：亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌为何玩不转游戏业务？
原创 作者：GR编译 22小时前 4.8k
作者按：亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌……这三家科技巨头拥有近乎无限的资金，却纷纷在游戏领域遭遇“惨败”。为什么许多公司总是犯同样的错误，似乎永远学不会吸取教训？在本篇文章中，笔者将会尝试解答这些问题。
如今，游戏产业已经成为全球营收最高的娱乐产业，年收入规模甚至超过了电影和音乐的总和。从理论上讲，对于那些已经运营着云基础架构、流媒体服务，或在全球电商市场占据较高份额的科技巨头来说，电子游戏(市场)本应是一个易于打开的关联市场，然而近年来，亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌投入巨资开展游戏业务，却几乎一无所获。结合具体数据来看，这三家公司在游戏领域的“战果”简直令人尴尬。
亚马逊：10年、年均投资5亿美元，零爆款
自从2012年成立以来，亚马逊游戏部门(Amazon Games)已经运营超过14年。据多家业内机构估计，在过去14年的大部分时间里，亚马逊每年都会为游戏业务投资约5亿美元。作为亚马逊的旗舰游戏，网游《新世界》(New World)历经5年开发，据估计耗资至少2亿美元。
2021年9月，《新世界》上线首日同时在线玩家数峰值超过90万。这个数字固然让人惊叹，但在随后的短短一年内，《新世界》的CCU峰值就暴跌到了仅数万。考虑到《新世界》是一款MMO，其长远表现显然没有达到亚马逊所期待的水平。
在游戏行业，头部MMO往往能够长期运营并持续吸金，然而，打造一款成功的MMO却极其困难。通过开发和运营《新世界》，亚马逊似乎想要亲自尝试一番，却未能收获成功。2025年10月，亚马逊宣布将停止为《新世界》开发后续内容，取消“指环王”IP衍生网游项目，并逐步撤离MMO领域。就在本月中旬，亚马逊还宣布会将两款韩国网游(《失落方舟》《王权与自由》)在欧美市场的发行权交还给开发商。
据媒体报道，在亚马逊内部，一个代号为“三叉戟”(Project Trident)的AI驱动游戏项目也被取消了，原因是管理层试图围绕生成式AI工具重组整个开发流程，而非专注于制作游戏……到2025年底，亚马逊基本上已经承认公司在游戏领域遭遇失败。在一轮波及超过14000人的大规模裁员中，亚马逊位于尔湾和圣迭戈的游戏部门遭受重创。亚马逊公开表示，其目标是彻底停止3A游戏和大型多人在线游戏的开发。作为一名玩家，笔者无法用语言表达对亚马逊这个决定的失望之情。
让我们来看看数据：2025年亚马逊的总收入达到了7170亿美元，就算每年投资5亿美元开展游戏业务，财务状况也不会受多大影响。然而尴尬的是，亚马逊已经在游戏行业耕耘十余年，手握的爆款数量却依然为0。作为比较，去年大热的《光与影：33号远征队》的开发预算仅为2000万美元，收入则已超过1.6亿美元。
亚马逊似乎始终没能真正理解，游戏的核心竞争力是创意，而非基础设施或交付速度。绝大多数游戏的制作过程甚至与技术无关——对开发者来说，现有工具已经够用了，他们不需要发明任何新技术。
在笔者看来，亚马逊也没有从波兰公司CDPR几年前的那次惨败中吸取教训：打造一款大型游戏需要耐心和经验，如果公司在缺乏经验的情况下盲目、激进地推进项目，或者急于求成，往往只会适得其反。2020年底，CDPR新作《赛博朋克2077》发售翻车，以至于投资者提起集体诉讼，指控被CDPR误导……当时，CDPR已经是一家广受赞誉的工作室，凭借“巫师”系列三部曲积累了丰富的游戏开发经验，却依然在触及自己不太熟悉的领域时遭遇了惨痛失败。
笔者认为，与其大幅收缩游戏业务，亚马逊或许更应思考公司是否聘请了合适的高管来领导游戏部门。亚马逊本应选择那些真正了解怎样才能在游戏行业赢得成功的人，并且不再死死地盯着电子表格，转而从艺术、创意和趣味的角度来看待游戏。如果亚马逊研究游戏行业的历史，还会意识到一味追随潮流，模仿热门游戏的做法行不通，打造独特、前卫、富有创意的作品方为成功之道。
Netflix：诊断正确，却开错了处方
与亚马逊相比，Netflix在游戏领域的失败更令人惋惜，因为他们起初颇有想法。早在2019年，这家流媒体巨头的联合创始人里德·哈斯廷斯(Reed Hastings)就告诉股东，Netflix的最大竞争对手并非HBO，而是《堡垒之夜》。这表明在当时，Netflix对用户如何度过闲暇时间有着非常敏锐的洞察力。然而，Netflix本应思考这样一个问题：“人们为什么玩《堡垒之夜》？”
上述问题的答案是“大逃杀”(battle royale)：一大群人涌入同一个地方，然后开始相互厮杀。时至今日，“大逃杀”概念仍然非常流行。有趣的是当《堡垒之夜》风靡全球时，Neflix出品了采用同一核心概念的韩剧《鱿鱼游戏》(2021年首播)。因此，对Netflix来说，制作更多采用类似主题的影视剧似乎是更合理的选择。
Netflix似乎从未思考过《堡垒之夜》为什么能够成功，却认定了自己与《堡垒之夜》为敌，要与后者争夺人们的闲暇时间……与此同时，Netflix高层还忽略了另一个关键事实：影视剧可以被动观看，游戏却需要人们主动游玩。人们可以躺在沙发上，半睡半醒地观看影视剧，玩游戏时却必须更加投入。
从某种意义上讲，Neflix确实可以将《堡垒之夜》视为竞争对手，但Netflix错就错在忽略了《堡垒之夜》成功背后的真正原因，以及看剧与玩游戏之间的巨大差异。
2021年11月，Netflix正式推出游戏订阅服务，面向订阅会员提供了一批无广告、无内购，可以免费畅玩的手游。然而，Netflix的目标是与游戏争抢用户的闲暇时间，却偏偏选择了自己制作手游，而非深耕以“大逃杀”叙事为核心的内容，投资制作更多剧集……Netflix没有积极寻找任何大逃杀风格的原创IP，而是宣布将推出一大堆手游。在笔者看来，Netflix本应继续利用“大逃杀”这个对影视剧观众和游戏玩家极具吸引力的概念，但Netflix高层似乎并没有意识到这一点。
根据移动应用数据分析和市场情报公司Apptopia的追踪数据显示，在Netflix游戏订阅服务上线至今的大约5年里，其月活跃用户数(MAU)于2023年1月达到峰值270万，占Netflix同期订阅会员总数(2.47亿)的比例低于1.1%。美国消费者新闻与商业频道(CNBC)也曾援引Apptopia数据，指出Netflix游戏的日活跃用户约为170万，占Netflix会员总数的比例不足1%。截至2023年底，Netflix数十款游戏的总下载量达到大约7050万次，平均下载量却很低，大多数游戏在iOS平台的每月下载量甚至从未超过5万次。
更糟的是，Netflix的游戏只能在移动设备上运行，却仅有大约10%的Netflix会员曾经使用智能手机看剧。换言之，Netflix为10%的用户打造游戏产品，赌的是“人人都有手机，都会尝试玩一玩”。但结果却并非如此。
除了位于芬兰的一家工作室之外(译注：Next Games），Netflix现已关闭公司旗下的大部分游戏工作室。这家流媒体服务提供商并没有完全放弃业务，但已经远离大型项目，如今正专注于寻找真正适合公司的游戏模式。2025年中，Netflix高管声称，自从公司将开发重心转向基于现有Netflix剧集的“互动叙事”游戏(如《艾米丽在巴黎》）以来，其游戏订阅服务的用户参与度同比增长了3倍。
笔者个人认为，Netflix或许可以考虑收购像Telltale这样的工作室，因为后者擅长制作叙事驱动型游戏，并且在开发IP衍生游戏方面拥有丰富经验，有能力帮助手握大量IP的Netflix在游戏领域赢得更大成功。
谷歌：承认失败，及时退场
与亚马逊和Netflix相比，谷歌似乎是更洒脱的失败者，因为在几年前，谷歌彻底取消了其雄心勃勃的游戏战略。2019年，谷歌推出云游戏服务平台Stadia，试图用它来取代家用游戏主机，但谷歌已于2023年1月彻底关闭该服务，并为购买游戏和硬件的用户提供了全额退款。
谷歌曾经在洛杉矶和蒙特利尔开设游戏研发工作室，但谷歌高管后来意识到，制作大型游戏所需要的时间、资金远远超出了他们的预期，并因此在短短18个月后就将第一方工作室关闭……谷歌的一位副总裁曾公开表示，Stadia“用户增长未能达到我们的预期”——考虑到谷歌的规模之大，这番话可谓相当直白。
有人可能会问，谷歌为什么不明白究竟怎样才能制作大型游戏？然而，亚马逊对此同样一知半解。两家公司的区别在于：谷歌很早就意识到了公司没有做游戏的基因，并果断“拔掉插头”，在相关投资变成长达10年的无底洞前及时止损。
如果将亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌在游戏行业的败局进行比较，你会发现，这三家科技巨头都犯过同样的错误。
1.亚马逊和谷歌将游戏开发视为一个规模化问题，使用构建云基础架构的方式来开发游戏：雇佣更多工程师，投入更多资金，以及更多的计算资源。但游戏开发是一门注重迭代的创作技艺，在很多时候，创作者的品味和感觉比资源更重要。
2.Netflix为了方便自己而设计游戏，却没有充分考虑用户玩游戏的实际场景。Netflix之所以面向订阅会员推出手游，原因是将手游集成到其现有应用中非常容易，公司高层想当然地认为用户愿意打开手机游玩……然而，Netflix的绝大多数用户却只想坐在沙发上看电视。
3.领导层毫无耐心。优秀的3A工作室通常需要7~10年时间，才能打造出一款真正的爆款游戏，但亚马逊游戏部门频繁更换高管，取消了多个大型项目，并且不断改变方向，从未给任何项目团队提供足够的时间。
4.他们高估了自家品牌的影响力，以为能轻松地将庞大用户群体转变成游戏玩家。然而，玩家与特定游戏和社群的联系往往更加紧密，并不会对发行商形成依赖。
总而言之，笔者认为亚马逊、Netflix和谷歌所遇到的问题都与游戏开发者的能力无关——领导层想当然地以为自己精通游戏业务，实则缺乏了解，这才是导致这些科技巨头在游戏领域遭遇失败的根本问题。
微软：真正“玩转”游戏业务的科技公司
笔者还想聊一聊微软。在游戏领域，微软并非从未遇到任何问题，但与其他科技巨头不同，微软没有试图从零开始制作爆款游戏，而是在过去十年间投入巨资，收购了一大批已经掌握打造爆款的方法论的工作室，包括《我的世界》开发商Mojang(2014年)、《上古卷轴》系列游戏开发商Bethesda的母公司ZeniMax(2021年)，以及手握《使命召唤》《魔兽世界》《暗黑破坏神》和《糖果传奇》等重磅IP的动视暴雪(2023年)等。迄今为止，微软已经为收购游戏工作室花费了大约800亿美元。
2024年2月，微软宣布游戏订阅服务Xbox Game Pass的订阅用户数已经达到大约3400万。过去十年间，微软的游戏业务年收入几乎翻了3倍，在收购动视暴雪后更是突破了200亿美元大关……微软并没有试图颠覆游戏行业，而是更倾向于收购已经在行业内深耕多年的团队，并放手让他们继续做自己最擅长的事情。
从某种意义上讲，这或许是微软最值得其他科技大厂学习的地方。（文/GR编译）
